issues.description: The problem statement's UML and textual parts contradict each other about the return type of messageOnMilk(): the class-level UML for animals (e.g. Seal, Goat) shows messageOnMilk() returning String, while the Milkable interface UML shows messageOnMilk():boolean. This inner inconsistency in the specification will confuse students about the correct type to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: choose a single return type for messageOnMilk() across all UML diagrams and textual descriptions. Update the Milkable interface UML and any textual references so they match the chosen type (either change the class-level UML and text to boolean, or change the Milkable UML and text to String). Prefer aligning the UML and text to the same return type to avoid student confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement's text explicitly instructs that messageOnMilk() should return a boolean (true if milking successful, false otherwise), but the provided solution implementation defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() returning String and the concrete animal classes (Seal, Goat) return Strings describing the milking. This cross-artifact mismatch will block or confuse students when implementing the interface to satisfy tests or the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Decide on the intended return type and align all artifacts. If the educational intent is to have messageOnMilk() return a String describing the milking (as in the reference solution), update the problem text and UML to state that messageOnMilk() returns String and provide example return values. If the intent is to use a boolean, change the solution's Milkable interface and all implementations to return boolean and update examples/tests accordingly.
